full_judgment:
2. The brief fact of the case is that the complainant opposite party filed petition of complaint before the Magistrate, 1st class Balagonj alleging that she got the suit property from her deceased father by way of inheritance and some portion by purchanse and the properties were duly recorded in her name. After receiving a notice under Section 30 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act complainant opposite party sent her son to the office of the settlement officer, where it was found that the petitioner and others in collusion with each other created a forged deed and produced a certified copy of the same before the settlement officer and got the property recorded in the name of the accused persons. Though the son of the complainant opposite party insisted for production of the original deed but the same was not produced, then after obtaining certified copy of the alleged deed the present complaint petition was filed. 

 5. We have perused the petition of complaint and the impugned order and considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates of respective parties. It appears from the petition of complaint that the accused petitioner while produced the certified copy of the alleged forged deed the son of the complainant insisted for production of the original deed before the settlement officer but the same was not Produced. So, we find from the petition of complaint that the original deed was neither submitted nor produced before the settlement officer. As the original deed was not produced before the settlement court, in our view provisions of section 195(I)(c) of the Code of Criminal procedure is not attracted. In section 195(I)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure the word "document" has been used. In our view document means and includes only the original document but not the certified copy. Our view is supported by decision in the case of Shamsuddin Ahmed Chowdhury versus State and another reported in 40 DLR(AD) page 159.
